content: Café au lait spots are pigmented birthmarks that appear on the skin. The term café au lait is derived from French, meaning coffee with milk, which describes their characteristic light-brown color in individuals with lighter skin tones. In individuals with darker skin, these spots may appear as darker lesions, sometimes referred to as café noir. From a pathophysiological perspective, café au lait spots are generally benign and not associated with medical conditions in most cases. However, the presence of multiple spots (three or more) can be indicative of underlying disorders such as neurofibromatosis or the rare McCune-Albright syndrome. Specifically, having six or more café au lait spots that are greater than 5 mm in diameter in prepubertal children or greater than 15 mm in diameter in postpubertal children is a key diagnostic criterion for Neurofibromatosis Type I.
